For example, Stripes in Stripe Delivery Center roles in Mexico City, Mexico, Bengaluru, India, and Dublin, Ireland work 100% from the office. Stripes on the Works in Progress team based in the London, UK office also work 100% from the office. Also, some teams have greater in-office attendance requirements, to appropriately support our users and workflows, which the hiring manager will discuss. This approach helps strike a balance between bringing people together for in-person collaboration and learning from each other, while supporting flexibility when possible. Pay and benefits The annual salary range for this role in the primary location is SGD 112,000 - SGD 168,000. This range may change if you are hired in another location. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings (“OTE”) range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. This salary range may be inclusive of several career levels at Stripe and will be narrowed during the interview process based on a number of factors, including the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and specific location. Applicants interested in this role and who are not located in the primary location may request the annual salary range for their location during the interview process. Specific benefits and details about what compensation is included in the salary range listed above will vary depending on the applicant’s location and can be discussed in more detail during the interview process. review_candidates.description: Role: Network Support Engineer Location: Salt Lake City, UT (Onsite) Duration: 12 Months Job Overview: We are seeking a Network Support Engineer with strong experience in enterprise networking, MPLS carrier networks, routing protocols, and network troubleshooting. The candidate will be responsible for maintaining network stability, resolving complex connectivity issues, monitoring network performance, and supporting 24/7 network operations. Key Responsibilities: Configure, monitor, and troubleshoot routers, switches, firewalls, access points, load balancers, and proxies. Troubleshoot Layer 3 private IP MPLS networks, BGP peering, and complex WAN architectures. Work with routing protocols including BGP, OSPF, EIGRP, and RIP. Analyze packet captures and network traffic to identify and resolve connectivity and performance issues. Troubleshoot WAN CE routers, QoS policies, carrier circuits, and network configurations. Monitor network alerts, investigate incidents, and coordinate resolution with management and support teams. Use tools such as Splunk, HPNA, Netdisco, Aruba Mobility Master, and EMC SMARTS for network monitoring and troubleshooting. Collaborate with data center technicians and vendors to resolve hardware issues involving ports, cables, modules, and network devices. Required Skills: Strong experience in networking, MPLS, BGP, OSPF, and EIGRP. Hands-on experience with Layer 3 routing and WAN troubleshooting. Knowledge of TCP/IP, SNMP, Multicast, VSS, STP, HSRP, and WAN switching. Experience with packet capture, traffic analysis, and network monitoring tools. Strong troubleshooting, incident management, and root cause analysis skills.

review_candidates.title: Director Hardware
review_candidates.description: Remote, LATAM SweatWorks was founded to make technology relevant, accessible, functional and beautiful so that our partners can engage their clients like never before. We believe in embracing and using technology to solve problems, not create new ones. SweatWorks has grown from a boutique fitness agency into a leading technology firm that is creating some of the most innovative experiences for exceptional brands. We are a force of digital strategists that create and implement extraordinary products for amazing clients. From startups to Fortune 500 companies, we work with clients to deliver digital solutions across web, mobile and all digital devices in between. From social networks to apps to complex content management systems, we have the capabilities to produce anything digital. WHAT WE OFFER Home-office-based role, offering flexibility and comfort Up to 15 paid vacation days per year Up to 5 floating holidays to celebrate the days that best reflect your culture and traditions Paid parental leaves for a special moment in your life Wellness days to ensure a healthy work-life balance Competitive health insurance coverage Reimbursement of internet and gym expenses Opportunities to work with leading brands in fitness and wellness Collaborating with a dynamic and diverse global team WHO THRIVES HERE People who thrive in this role are hands-on leaders who are comfortable creating clarity in environments that are still evolving. They combine strong technical judgment with a high level of ownership, translating ambiguity into priorities, decisions, and momentum for the team. They enjoy building—not only hardware products, but also the processes, standards, and ways of working that make delivery more predictable and scalable. They communicate early, surface risks before they become blockers, and collaborate naturally across Hardware, Software, Product, Design, QA, Operations, Leadership, clients, and external partners. They are technically credible without needing to own every decision themselves. They develop strong teams by setting clear expectations, creating autonomy, giving timely feedback, and stepping into the details when the situation requires it. Most importantly, they understand that successful hardware leadership requires balancing engineering excellence with manufacturability, timelines, cost, client expectations, and business outcomes. ABOUT OUR HIRING PROCESS Interview with HR Interview with Operations Manager Interview with C-Level Job Offer THE ROLE WHAT YOU'LL BE DOING As Hardware Director, you’ll be responsible for the overall performance and evolution of SweatWorks’ hardware function across active programs and future opportunities. You’ll oversee how hardware initiatives move from early scoping through manufacturing and delivery, ensuring the right coordination across internal teams, our China-based operations, suppliers, and manufacturing partners. You’ll also strengthen the systems, partnerships, and operating practices needed to support reliable delivery as the hardware portfolio grows. Beyond program execution, you’ll play an important role in the commercial side of the business—supporting new opportunities, contributing to feasibility and planning decisions, and representing the Hardware function in key client and leadership conversations. RESPONSIBILITIES Lead the hardware function and drive performance Lead the Hardware department across delivery, product quality, program margin, and client satisfaction. Define the team's operating rhythm, priorities, KPIs, and ways of working, creating visibility for Leadership across active programs. Plan team capacity and future hiring needs so the department can support new programs while maintaining delivery quality. Lead, coach, and develop the hardware team, keeping hardware strategy, manufacturing, and program execution aligned. Build strong vendor and manufacturing partnerships Lead commercial negotiations with contract manufacturers, component suppliers, and tooling partners, including pricing, MOQs, payment terms, tooling ownership, and quality agreements. Identify and qualify new OEM/ODM partners as the hardware pipeline grows, while maintaining reliable backup options for critical suppliers. Oversee vendor performance and step into escalations or disputes when needed, while Project Operations manages day-to-day supplier, factory, and logistics coordination. Partner with commercial leadership on contracts and SOWs for hardware programs, including warranty, liability, and supply commitments. Lead our China team and manufacturing operations Directly lead our China-based engineering, firmware, R&D, and production team, setting priorities, creating accountability, and developing the team's capabilities. Oversee the full path from prototype to mass production, including DFM reviews, EVT/DVT/PVT gates, certifications, and production ramp. Manage supply chain forecasting, inventory planning, and component lifecycle risks, including EOL planning. Travel to factories and strategic partners when needed to support production readiness, audits, problem-solving, and relationship building. Support growth and shape new hardware opportunities Partner with the Growth team to evaluate new hardware opportunities, including technical feasibility, cost, timelines, manufacturing complexity, and delivery risk. Help shape realistic scopes and solutions before commitments are made to clients. Represent SweatWorks Hardware in senior client conversations, building trust, explaining technical trade-offs clearly, and setting realistic expectations from the start. YOUR SKILLS WHAT WE REQUIRE 5+ years in hardware product development, with at least 3 years leading a hardware team or department. A track record of taking consumer or commercial electronics from prototype to mass production. Direct experience managing contract manufacturers and suppliers in China, including negotiating cost, terms, and tooling. Experience managing distributed or cross-cultural teams across time zones. Strong commercial judgment: you can read a BOM, a quote, and a contract, and you know where the margin and the risk sit. Clear, direct communication with executives, clients, and factory partners alike. WILL BE A PLUS Experience in connected fitness, smart equipment, or other IoT products. Background with tablet-based or embedded Android devices, firmware, and MDM. Agency or client-services experience: running several client programs at once. Working knowledge of certifications (FCC, CE, UL, and similar). Mandarin language skills. Does it sound like you? APPLY NOW! Please note: Only applications submitted in English will be considered. This is a direct hire opportunity. Third-party vendors, staffing firms, and recruitment agencies are kindly asked to refrain from contacting us regarding this position.
